transcript.text: Early in the afternoon, on March 21st, 22, officers from the Pleasant Prairie Police Department near Kenosha, Wisconsin discovered a vehicle was stolen after running plates. The driver of the squad is a rookie officer. During the course of the video, you will hear the rookie's training officer giving him instructions throughout the chase. At this time, more officers join the pursuit. The stolen vehicle now has multiple police squads on their attention. As the driver continues to evade, police officers coordinate to set up a stopstick trap at the end of the road. The stopstick trap is a success, hitting both the front and rear tires of the vehicle deflating them. The driver continues the pursuit regardless. However, officers have a second stopstick trap set up further down the road in preparation. In an attempt to avoid the stopsticks, the driver swerves out of control crashing on the side of the street, giving officers a chance to detain the driver. I'm going to the vehicle! Roll it. Go ahead and roll to your side. No, just help. Just get me up. Bring your knees up. Bring your knees up to your chest. Bring your knees to your chest. This stuff hurt. Bring your knees to your chest, man. I'm just checking your handcuffs so they don't tighten down on you. They're too tight. No, they're not, because you can spin your hand so you're fine. Can y'all get my phone, my ID, and my money? In my arms, my bags, I need everything out that car. What's up there, guy? According to police reports, when the owner of the vehicle was informed of who stole their car, it was found that the driver actually knew the thief as an acquaintance. The driver was charged as an operator fleeing an officer, and causing damage, with second-degree recklessly endangering safety, of driving a vehicle without the owner's consent, and with having possession of THC. Reckless endangerment and possession of THC were both dismissed on the prosecutor's motion. For fleeing an officer and driving without the owner's consent, she was found guilty due to a guilty plea. For this, she was ordered to pay a restitution of $2,650. She also had her Department of Transportation license revoked for one year, and she received two years of probation, but that was withheld and would go into effect if the defendant were to commit another crime. That's the chase. And in my opinion, really a pretty good job by both the rookie officer and the FTO has field training officer. The field training officer, staying on top of the rookie, making sure that no mistakes are made. This was a chase of a stolen car, which is really a property crime. A lot of agencies will no longer allow for a chase of a stolen car unless there's also a violent crime associated with it, like a gun crime or carjacking. But there are differing opinions in law enforcement about this. A stolen car, even though it's just a property crime, it tends to be a sign that the offender is going to go on to commit a more violent crime because it's an anonymous car. So conflicting opinions about whether you should chase or should not chase a stolen vehicle. On one hand, it's a property crime. But on the other hand, it's a property crime that tends to lead to violent crimes or gun violence.
